convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to invoke 'Bezier' custom indicator (not a built-in MT5 indicator), and includes external TradeAlgorithms.mqh library for position management. The Bezier indicator logic is unavailable without its source, requiring manual Python reimplementation of the Bezier calculation. TradeAlgorithms.mqh functions also need manual porting.

derived_values.name: Bezier buffer values [0],[1],[2]
derived_values.formula: CopyBuffer(InpInd_Handle, 0, SignalBar, 3, Value) — three consecutive Bezier values at bars SignalBar, SignalBar+1, SignalBar+2

other_exits: Long position closed when Bezier[SignalBar+1] > Bezier[SignalBar+2] (downturn detected) and BuyPosClose is true
Short position closed when Bezier[SignalBar+1] < Bezier[SignalBar+2] (upturn detected) and SellPosClose is true

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MM<0 means fixed lot size = abs(MM); MM>0 means deposit fraction

custom_logic_notes: The Bezier indicator is a custom smoothing indicator using Bézier curve interpolation with a sensitivity parameter T (0-1). The entry logic compares three consecutive Bezier values: if Value[1]<Value[2] (was declining) AND Value[0]>Value[1] (now rising), it's a buy signal (trend reversal up). If Value[1]>Value[2] (was rising) AND Value[0]<Value[1] (now declining), it's a sell signal (trend reversal down). SignalBar=1 means signals are evaluated on the most recently closed bar. The EA uses static variables to persist signals across ticks until a new bar fires. BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/BuyPosClose/SellPosClose are input toggles that gate each action independently. TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, LoadHistory, GlobalVariableDel_, and CIsNewBar helper functions.
python_conversion_notes: 1) The Bezier custom indicator must be reimplemented in Python — it uses Bézier curve smoothing with period and sensitivity parameters applied to a weighted price. Without the indicator source code, approximate using a polynomial regression or Savitzky-Golay filter with equivalent smoothing. 2) TradeAlgorithms.mqh functions need manual porting: position open/close with lot sizing from deposit fraction (MM parameter: negative=fixed lot, positive=deposit fraction), stop loss/take profit in points, and slippage control. 3) The IsNewBar guard means signals are evaluated once per completed bar — replicate with bar-time tracking in Python. 4) Entry logic is a directional change detection: Bezier turns up → buy, Bezier turns down → sell. 5) StopLoss and TakeProfit are in points (1000 and 2000 respectively), need conversion to price distance using point_value. 6) Deviation=10 is max slippage in points.
